newsitem.title: UK: Ukraine steps into international capital market.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine steps into international capital market.

text.p: Ukraine, an unrated sovereign borrower, took its first step in the international capital markets on Monday with a well-received $450 million one-year note issue.
The notes, which will not pay a coupon but were issued at a discounted price, will raise around $410 million to be used for general budgetary purposes.
"This issue is the crucial first step in establishing Ukraine in the international capital markets and in diversifying our funding sources," Finance Minister Ihor Mityukov said in a statement.
"We intend to continue to develop our capital markets programme, obtaining credit ratings, extending maturities and diversifying currencies."
Ukraine was the only major Eastern European sovereign borrower which had not yet tapped international capital markets.

The $450 million in notes, underwritten by Nomura International, were issued on a fiduciary basis by Bankers Trust Luxembourg SA. This structure, previously used for borrowers such as the City of Prague, gives bondholders extra protection, bankers said.

"If the tax law should change regarding Ukraine's debt, for example, bondholders are protected due to the fiduciary structure," a debt dealer said. "Bankers Trust is responsible for repaying the debt."
The transaction was well-received by investors, despite the lack of comparable deals in the market, dealers said.
"We have seen good demand, despite no real benchmark to compare it to," a banker involved in the transaction said. "It is short-dated sovereign paper, and a liquid deal, and has been snapped up."
An official at Nomura said initial demand had been strong and investors who had already been active in the domestic T-bill market were buyers.

"Investors involved in Ukraine T-bills will get involved in this transaction. We have seen demand from retail, Austrian and German banks and Middle Eastern buyers and expect to see wider buying as credit lines are opened for Ukraine," he said.
The notes were priced to yield 3.25 percentage points over one-year dollar Libor, which on Monday was at 6.125 percent.
Ukraine is due to issue two more international bonds which could raise up to $1 billion and is in the process of obtaining international credit ratings.
It has appointed Nomura to underwrite a bond in the yen market in September and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and J.P. Morgan to underwrite a dollar deal.
The former Soviet republic, which gained independence in 1992, is implementing structural reforms to turn around its economy.
"This is one element of our larger programme to enhance foreign investment flows to Ukraine, to support the continuation of our economic reform programme," Mityukov said in the statement.
Last week Ukraine signed a standby agreement with the International Monetary Fund and said it expected to receive $700-$800 million from the IMF by the end of the year.
The agreement is designed to see Ukraine through an interim period while it implements its structural reforms and could be followed by an extended loan.

"The (note) issue presents the first opportunity for investors to obtain sovereign exposure to Ukraine in standard Eurobond format," Dan Jackson, deputy managing director for European emerging markets at Nomura, said.

"It should greatly enhance awareness of Ukraine's impressive macroeconomic stabilisation, which has brought inflation from hyper-inflation levels in 1993 to 5.4 percent in the first seven months of 1997." -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7748
